ai-copilot.name: AI Copilot
ai-copilot.h1: The AI tutor that knows your curriculum.
ai-copilot.sub: Copilot gives every student patient, step-by-step help grounded in your course material — 24/7, in 20+ languages.

sections.title: Grounded in your content, not the open web
sections.body: Every answer is retrieved from the courses your school has loaded, and shown with the chapter it came from. When Copilot does not know, it says so and points the student to their teacher.
points: Answers cite the source chapter or resource
No answers invented from outside your material
Teachers can see and audit every conversation

sections.title: Adapts to each learner
sections.body: Copilot reads where a student is stuck and adjusts explanation, vocabulary and pace — the same concept explained three different ways for three different learners.
points: Level-aware explanations, from foundation to extension
Follows the learner’s language preference automatically
Suggests the next step rather than handing over answers

sections.title: Safe by design
sections.body: Age-appropriate responses, monitored conversations, keyword flagging to safeguarding leads, and a hard rule: your school’s data is never used to train models.
points: Safeguarding alerts routed to your designated lead
No training on your data — contractually

sections.title: Teacher controls
sections.body: Teachers decide what Copilot can discuss, when it is available, and how much help it gives during assessment. It is an assistant to the teacher, not a replacement for one.
points: Adjustable help level, from hints to full worked examples
Visibility of the questions students are actually asking

faq.q: Can Copilot just do students’ homework for them?
faq.a: Teachers set the help level. In assessment mode Copilot offers hints and questions rather than answers, and every conversation is visible to staff.

faq.q: Which languages does it support?
faq.a: The same 20+ languages as the platform, including right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Urdu. A student can ask in their home language about an English-language course.

faq.q: Is our content used to train your models?
faq.a: No. Your course material and student conversations are never used for model training. This is written into the data-processing agreement.

simulations.name: Interactive Simulations
simulations.h1: Science and maths you can touch.
simulations.sub: 20+ interactive simulations across physics, chemistry, maths and biology — hands-on learning that makes concepts stick.

sections.title: Browse by subject
sections.body: Projectile motion, circuit building, molecule shapes, balancing equations, natural selection, graphing — organised by subject and mapped to the topics you already teach.
points: Mapped to Cambridge and Edexcel topics
Filter by year group and difficulty

sections.title: Embedded, full-screen, mobile-ready
sections.body: Drop a simulation into any lesson, open it full-screen on the projector, or let students explore it on a phone on the bus home. Same simulation, every device.

sections.title: Pair with lessons and Copilot
sections.body: A simulation next to a Copilot conversation turns exploration into understanding — students can ask "why did that happen?" the moment it happens.
points: Attach guiding questions to any simulation

sections.title: Built on trusted, research-backed simulations
sections.body: Our science simulations build on PhET Interactive Simulations from the University of Colorado Boulder — decades of education research, not a novelty.

faq.q: Do simulations work offline?
faq.a: Simulations need a connection to load, but run entirely in the browser afterwards — they hold up on the patchy school Wi-Fi at the back of a science block.

faq.q: Can we request a simulation we need?
faq.a: Yes. Playgrounds lets teachers generate an interactive activity for any topic, and we build requested simulations into the core library on a rolling basis.

courses.name: Courses & Curriculum
courses.sub: Structured courses aligned to Cambridge and Edexcel — or build your own, with AI doing the heavy lifting.

sections.title: A ready-made library
sections.body: Courses across the core subjects, structured into units, lessons and assessments — usable on the first day of term, not the first day of next year.
points: Core subjects covered at each key stage

sections.title: Aligned to learning objectives and past papers
sections.body: Every lesson maps to specification points and assessment objectives, with past-paper style practice attached so revision is not a separate workflow.

sections.title: Author your own courses
sections.body: Your best teachers already have the material. Bring it in, and AI structures it into lessons, generates questions and fills the gaps you point at.

sections.title: Collections, pathways and media
sections.body: Group courses into pathways for a year group, an intervention cohort or a summer school — and include podcasts, video and reading alongside interactive work.

faq.q: Can we bring our own schemes of work?
faq.a: Yes — that is the normal path. Most schools import existing material during onboarding and let the platform structure it, rather than starting from scratch.

faq.q: Who owns the content we author?
faq.a: You do. Content your staff create stays yours, and you can export it at any time.

playgrounds.name: Playgrounds
playgrounds.h1: Generate an interactive lesson in minutes.
playgrounds.sub: Describe a topic; Playgrounds builds an interactive, AI-generated experience your students can explore.

sections.title: From prompt to activity
sections.body: Type what you want students to understand. Playgrounds generates an interactive activity — a model, a sorter, a simulation, a scenario — in the time it takes to make a coffee.

sections.title: Examples by subject
sections.body: A supply-and-demand model for economics, a titration walkthrough for chemistry, a sentence-structure builder for languages — the range is the point.
points: Works across humanities, sciences and languages

sections.title: Teacher in control
sections.body: Nothing generated goes live automatically. You review, edit and approve — then share to a class, a set or a single student who needs a different angle.

sections.title: Share to a class
sections.body: One click to a class, a group or an individual, with progress tracked in the same dashboards as everything else.
points: Share to class, group or student

faq.q: How accurate is generated content?
faq.a: Playgrounds drafts; teachers approve. Nothing reaches students without a member of staff reviewing it, which is exactly where professional judgement belongs.

community.name: Community & Collaboration
community.sub: Moderated communities and discussions that keep students connected to their class and teachers.

sections.title: Class and subject communities
sections.body: A space per class and per subject where questions get asked out loud — including the ones students would never raise with their hand up.

sections.title: Moderated discussions
sections.body: Automated moderation plus human oversight. Flagged content routes to the right member of staff with the context attached.

sections.title: Announcements
sections.body: Reach a class, a year group or the whole school without adding another messaging app to the pile.

sections.title: Safeguarding controls
sections.body: Direct messaging policy, keyword alerting, retention rules and reporting — configured to your safeguarding policy, not ours.

faq.q: Can students message each other privately?
faq.a: Only if your school enables it. Many schools run communities with peer-to-peer DMs disabled entirely; the setting is yours.

analytics.name: Progress & Analytics
analytics.h1: See how every learner is really doing.
analytics.sub: Dashboards for students, teachers and leaders — plus certificates that prove completion.

sections.title: Student progress & trails
sections.body: Every student sees where they are, what is next and what they have mastered — progress as motivation, not surveillance.

sections.title: Teacher class views
sections.body: One screen per class showing who is thriving, who is stuck and where the whole group has misunderstood the same thing.

sections.title: Leadership dashboards
sections.body: Attainment, engagement and platform adoption across departments and year groups — the whole-school view that spreadsheets never gave you.

sections.title: Certificates, export & reporting
sections.body: Completion certificates for students, and clean exports for your MIS, governors’ reports and inspection evidence.

faq.q: Does it integrate with our MIS?
faq.a: Data exports via CSV and API are available on every plan; direct MIS integrations are scoped as part of Enterprise onboarding.

white-label.name: White-label & Branding
white-label.sub: Your logo, colours, name and domain — a platform families recognise as yours, in 20+ languages.

sections.title: Full brand control
sections.body: Logo, palette, typography and tone applied across the platform — web, email and certificates. Students see their school, not a vendor.

sections.title: Custom domain
sections.body: Runs on your domain — learn.yourschool.org — with certificates and DNS handled during onboarding.

sections.title: 20+ languages including RTL
sections.body: Interface and content available in over 20 languages, with genuine right-to-left support for Arabic and Urdu — mirrored layouts, not flipped text.

sections.title: Single sign-on
sections.body: Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace, so nobody manages another password and offboarding a leaver actually removes their access.

faq.q: Will anyone know it’s RacoLearnHub?
faq.a: Not from the interface. The platform carries your identity throughout; ours appears only in the contract.

payments.name: Payments & Admin
payments.sub: Collect tuition and fees, track payments, and manage your school — without the spreadsheets.

sections.title: Fee collection & history
sections.body: Take payments for tuition, trips and materials, with a full history per family and per student in the same place as everything else.

sections.title: Automated reminders
sections.body: Polite, automatic reminders on your schedule — so chasing fees stops being a person’s job.

sections.title: Roles & permissions
sections.body: Granular permissions so finance sees finance, teaching sees teaching, and the audit trail shows who changed what.

sections.title: Enrolment & reporting
sections.body: Manage enrolment through the year and report on it without exporting three systems into a spreadsheet first.

faq.q: Which payment providers do you support?
faq.a: Payment provider options depend on your country and are confirmed during onboarding — this is one to raise on your demo call.

leaders.name: For School Leaders
leaders.h1: Raise attainment. Save staff time. See everything.
leaders.sub: One accountable platform that lifts outcomes, gives teachers their time back, and gives you a live view of your whole school.

sections.title: The leadership case
sections.body: Attainment, efficiency and oversight in one business case: better outcomes for students, hours back for staff, and a single accountable supplier instead of five.
points: One contract, one supplier, one bill

sections.title: Live analytics
sections.body: Whole-school dashboards updated continuously — by department, year group and cohort — so governors’ reports write themselves.

sections.title: Safeguarding & compliance
sections.body: GDPR-aligned, UK/EU hosted, with safeguarding controls and audit trails that satisfy your DSL and your DPO.

sections.title: Consolidate tools & cost
sections.body: One platform retires the tutoring app, the video library, the quiz tool and the fee spreadsheet — which is usually where the budget comes from.

sections.title: Rollout & support
sections.body: A named partner through onboarding, staff training built into the plan, and support that answers before the lesson is over.

faq.q: How long does rollout take?
faq.a: Most single schools are teaching on the platform within a half-term: branding and course import first, then staff training, then students.

faq.q: What does this replace?
faq.a: Typically a tutoring or homework app, a video/content library, a quiz or assessment tool, and a fee-tracking spreadsheet — sometimes an LMS as well.

teachers.name: For Teachers
teachers.h1: Spend less time on admin. More time teaching.
teachers.sub: Curriculum-ready content, AI that differentiates for you, and a tutor that answers the questions you can’t get to.

sections.title: A week in the life — before and after
sections.body: Before: three evenings on resources, a weekend on differentiation, and a queue of students you never reached. After: content that is already aligned, differentiation generated, and questions answered while you sleep.
points: Resources ready, not built from scratch
The quiet questions finally get asked

sections.title: Differentiation made easy
sections.body: One lesson, three levels, automatically — foundation, core and extension generated from the same material and assigned in a click.
points: Assign per student or per group
Adjust anything before it goes out

sections.title: Copilot as your teaching assistant
sections.body: Copilot handles the twentieth "can you explain that again?" so you can spend the lesson on the students who need you in the room.
points: Shows what the class is stuck on

sections.title: Build & share in minutes
sections.body: Playgrounds turns a topic description into an interactive activity, ready to review and share to your class before the bell.

sections.title: Track your class
sections.body: One screen showing who is thriving, who is stuck, and which misconception the whole group shares.

faq.q: How much training will I need?
faq.a: Most teachers are running lessons after a single session. The platform is designed to be usable before it is mastered.

faq.q: Does the AI mark my students’ work?
faq.a: It drafts and suggests; you decide. Professional judgement stays with the teacher, by design.

students.name: For Students & Parents
students.h1: Help whenever you need it, in your language.
students.sub: A personal AI tutor, interactive lessons, and a place to learn that works on any device.

sections.title: Learn your way
sections.body: Read it, watch it, try it or ask about it. The same topic, in whichever form finally makes it click.
points: Pick up where you left off, on any device

sections.title: Never stuck for long
sections.body: Copilot explains things as many times as you need, in as many ways as it takes — without anyone sighing.

sections.title: Fun, hands-on simulations
sections.body: Drop a ball, build a circuit, balance an equation. Some things you only understand once you have broken them.

sections.title: For parents: visibility & peace of mind
sections.body: See what your child is learning and how they are getting on — and know the platform is monitored, age-appropriate and run by their school.

sections.title: Accessible & multilingual
sections.body: Built to WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard-operable, screen-reader friendly, and available in 20+ languages including right-to-left.

faq.q: Can I sign up myself?
faq.a: RacoLearnHub is provided by schools rather than sold to families directly — ask your school whether they use it, or point them our way.

faq.q: Is it safe?
faq.a: Conversations are monitored, content is age-appropriate, and your school controls the settings. Student data is never used to train AI models.

trusts.name: For Trusts & School Groups
trusts.h1: One platform across every school in your trust.
trusts.sub: Standardise quality, compare across schools, and buy once — with per-school branding and central oversight.

sections.title: Central + per-school control
sections.body: Set standards centrally, let each school keep its own identity. Shared curriculum, separate front doors.

sections.title: Cross-school analytics
sections.body: Compare attainment, engagement and adoption across your schools — and see which practice is worth spreading.

sections.title: Procurement made simple
sections.body: One contract, one security review, one invoice — with the documentation your procurement team asks for up front.

sections.title: Volume pricing
sections.body: Pricing that reflects the size of your estate, with predictable per-student economics as schools join.

sections.title: Dedicated partnership
sections.body: A named team, a rollout plan per school, and an SLA that matches the scale of the commitment.

faq.q: Can schools join in phases?
faq.a: Yes — most trusts start with two or three schools, prove the model, then extend across the estate at the start of an academic year.

faq.q: Can each school keep its own branding?
faq.a: Yes. Central standards and per-school identity are not in tension here: schools keep their own look, domain and voice.

faq.q: Where is our data hosted?
faq.a: In the UK/EU by default, with documented residency. International schools can discuss regional hosting during procurement.

faq.q: Do you train AI models on our data?
faq.a: No. Course content and student conversations are never used for model training, and this is written into the data-processing agreement rather than only stated on a website.

faq.q: Can we see your security documentation?
faq.a: Yes — request the security pack below. It includes policies, the sub-processor list, a penetration-test summary and our data-processing agreement.

faq.q: How do you handle safeguarding incidents?
faq.a: Flagged content routes to your named safeguarding lead with full context. Escalation paths, retention and reporting are configured to your school’s policy.

faq.q: What is your accessibility standard?
faq.a: We target WCAG 2.2 AA across the product and this marketing site, and publish an accessibility statement schools can reference in their own compliance reporting.

faq.q: What happens to our data if we leave?
faq.a: You can export your content and records at any time. On termination, data is deleted according to the schedule in the agreement.

hero.title: Built by an AI lab that believes in teachers.
hero.sub: RacoLearnHub is made by RACO AI Technologies — a UK AI lab building AI that works for people, not instead of them.

mission.title: Technology should give teachers time, not take it.
paragraphs: RACO AI Technologies is an AI lab and engineering company. We build applied AI products — and RacoLearnHub is the one we care about most, because education is where the compounding happens.

We started it after watching the same pattern in school after school: enormous effort spent stitching tools together, and the students who most needed help still waiting for a moment of a teacher’s attention that never came.
Our position is unfashionable and simple. AI should not replace the teacher. It should handle the twentieth repetition of the same explanation, so the teacher can do the thing only a human can.
mission.cardBody: Because a tutor for every child used to be a question of wealth. It does not have to be any more — and a school-controlled platform, rather than a consumer app, is the way that happens safely.
cardItems: Schools own their content and their data
